claims.quote: It was close to midnight when I went back to the library.
Outside the window the little loop of metal and the short cord lay where Mary had said they were, tucked low in the ivy so you missed them if you were not looking for them.
There were no measured dimensions, no forensic photographs I could consult; there was only what the hand could feel and the eye could test.
I threaded a spare cord through the loop and tied it to the heft of the opener.

The letter-opener was the sort of blunt brass thing Lena kept for estate envelopes — heavy in a way that made it obedient to a short swing, as long as my palm and thick enough that the haft filled the hand.
It carried the same thin smear of oil along the haft that we had noted in the room; the oil caught the light like a small confession.
Balancing the opener on a short tag of cord, I pushed the sash just enough to take the tiniest of gaps.
From sash to thrust to withdrawal and the final pull that set the glass neat again: less than a minute.
I ran the test twice, and on the second try I let the opener bite into a pad of cloth I had tucked against the sash to simulate flesh.
The oil on the haft smeared on the cloth in a way that looked right.
'You shouldn't be here,' Oliver said, hard enough that the name would have been the sort of thing you bark when you meant a threat.
A hand closed on my wrist with a pressure that was not quite friendly;
He smelled of cold earth and tobacco.
His other hand went for the loop and began to wind the cord away as if he meant to make the thing vanish while I still had fingers on it.
I would bring Milne back before daylight and stage the thing properly.
The locked-room was not yet explained; it was something to be proved.
The loop's exact attachment — whether it had been tied to a screw, hooked, or simply tucked in — was not written in the file.

promises.promise: Crowe will bring Inspector Milne back before daylight and stage the pulley-and-opener demonstration with notebook and camera present, to prove whether the mechanism could explain the locked-room appearance.
